items.name: Santa Cruz Beach Boardwalk
items.cost: Free admission; rides and attractions paid; parking paid in Boardwalk lots
items.description: Seaside amusement park on Beach Street next to Main Beach, with rides, arcades and games; entry is free and you pay for rides and parking.
items.notes: Entry is free; rides and games are ticketed. Ride days and hours change with the season: check the Boardwalk's calendar.

items.name: Santa Cruz Wharf
items.cost: Free to walk; parking $3/hour summer ($24 max), $1/hour first 4 hours in winter ($12 max)
items.best_time: Tuesdays: 2 hours free parking with a validation stamp from any wharf business; Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's Day parking is free.
items.description: City-owned wharf with dining, shopping and recreation, beside Cowell and Main beaches.
items.notes: Only service dogs on the wharf. The City is repairing the wharf's end, and the wharf closes during high surf.

items.name: West Cliff Drive
items.address: W Cliff Dr, Santa Cruz, CA 95060
items.best_time: Sunset; low-tide or big-swell days to watch surfers at the point.
items.description: About 2.5 miles of wheelchair-accessible coastal multi-use path running from near the Wharf and Boardwalk to Natural Bridges, passing the lighthouse and surfing museum.
items.notes: Dogs on leash. The City plans path work near Lighthouse Point from late 2026 and roadway work near Lighthouse Field from June to December 2027; expect detours.

items.name: Santa Cruz Surfing Museum (Mark Abbott Memorial Lighthouse)
items.address: 701 West Cliff Drive, Santa Cruz, CA 95060
items.hours: Thu–Mon 12:30–4:30 PM (Labor Day–Memorial Day); 12:30–5:30 PM in summer; closed Tue & Wed
items.description: Small museum inside the lighthouse at Lighthouse Point overlooking Steamer Lane, with photos, surfboards and artifacts covering over 100 years of Santa Cruz surfing.
items.notes: No admission price is listed; the museum relies on donations.

items.name: Santa Cruz Mission State Historic Park
items.hours: Thu, Fri, Sat & Mon 10 AM–4 PM
items.description: Restored adobe on Mission Hill, the last remaining building of California's 12th mission, with exhibits interpreting the site through Ohlone and Yokuts experiences.
items.notes: Closed Thanksgiving and Christmas Day. Dogs on the grounds, not in the building.

items.name: Mystery Spot
items.address: 465 Mystery Spot Road, Santa Cruz, CA 95065
items.cost: Parking $5.00 per vehicle; tour ticket price not published on homepage
items.hours: Mon–Fri 10 AM–4 PM; Sat–Sun 10 AM–5 PM; tours every half hour
items.best_time: Buy tickets in advance, especially in summer; weekend and holiday slots often sell out around noon. Arrive 30 minutes before tour time.
items.description: Privately run attraction on Mystery Spot Road, seen on guided tours that leave every half hour.
items.notes: Parking is $5 a vehicle; the ticket price isn't on the homepage.

items.name: Seymour Marine Discovery Center
items.description: UC Santa Cruz's community-supported marine science education center.
items.notes: Ticket prices vary by age and aren't published on the page; under-3s free.

items.name: Monterey Bay National Marine Sanctuary Exploration Center
items.best_time: Wednesdays 10–11 a.m. for free Toddler Time.
items.description: NOAA visitor center with interactive exhibits on the sanctuary, including a kelp forest display and an 18-foot-wide theater screen.
items.notes: Guided tours run by reservation.

items.name: Natural Bridges State Beach
items.address: Natural Bridges State Beach, Santa Cruz, CA
items.best_time: Monarchs: late October through November is often best (season mid-Oct to mid-Feb). Tidepools at tides of 2 ft or lower.
items.description: State beach at the west end of West Cliff Drive with a monarch butterfly overwintering grove and tidepools in a Marine Protected Area.
items.notes: Visitor center open daily Oct 1–Jan 31, Fri–Mon Feb 1–Sep 30. No dogs on beach or trails; no drones, fires or glass on the beach; no touching or collecting in tidepools; no lifeguards.

items.name: Cowell Beach
items.hours: Closed midnight to one hour before sunrise
items.best_time: Lifeguards daily Memorial Day–Labor Day 10 AM–7 PM; weekends in spring and fall.
items.description: City beach at the Wharf where non-motorized craft such as paddleboards may launch from the far west end, at the lifeguard's discretion.
items.notes: No dogs, alcohol, smoking, glass or campfires on city beaches.

items.name: Main Beach
items.best_time: Lifeguards daily Memorial Day–Labor Day 10 AM–7 PM; weekends in spring and fall.
items.description: City beach on Beach Street in the lifeguarded stretch between Cowell Beach and the San Lorenzo River, with 18 volleyball courts.
items.notes: No dogs, alcohol, smoking, glass or campfires on city beaches.

items.name: Lighthouse Field State Beach & Steamer Lane
items.address: Lighthouse Field State Beach & Steamer Lane, Santa Cruz, CA
items.hours: 6 a.m. to sunset; parking lot 8 a.m. to sunset
items.description: State beach on West Cliff Drive around the lighthouse at Lighthouse Point, overlooking the Steamer Lane surf break.
items.notes: One of few local beaches where leashed dogs (6 ft max) are allowed, including on the beach.

items.name: Mitchell's Cove Beach
items.address: West Cliff Drive, Santa Cruz, CA 95060
items.best_time: Dog owners: off-leash allowed before 10 am and after 4 pm.
items.description: Small beach below West Cliff Drive reached by a stairway at Sunset Avenue, with off-leash dog hours.

items.name: Twin Lakes State Beach
items.address: Twin Lakes State Beach, Santa Cruz, CA
items.description: Mile-long sandy beach along East Cliff Drive on both sides of the Santa Cruz small craft harbor, next to Schwan Lake for birdwatching.
items.notes: State Parks doesn't publish hours or fees for it ((831) 427-4868). Leashed dogs on the east side of the harbor.

items.name: Pleasure Point County Park
items.address: East Cliff Drive, Santa Cruz, CA 95062
items.description: Small county park and vista point on East Cliff Drive with coastal and surf access, outdoor showers and the East Cliff County Parkway path.

items.name: Henry Cowell Redwoods State Park
items.address: 101 Big Trees Park Rd., Felton, CA 95018
items.hours: Sunrise to sunset; visitor center 10am–4pm daily
items.description: Redwood park whose flat 0.8-mile Redwood Grove Loop passes old-growth trees up to about 277 feet tall, including the walk-in Fremont Tree.
items.notes: No dogs on the Redwood Grove Loop; no drones.

items.name: Wilder Ranch State Park
items.address: Wilder Ranch State Park, Santa Cruz, CA
items.description: Coastal park just north of Santa Cruz with a historic ranch complex (1897 Victorian home, 1896 water-powered machine shop) and more than 35 miles of trails.
items.notes: No dogs; no drones. The park store is closed after flooding.

items.name: Pogonip Open Space Preserve
items.address: 501 and 410 Golf Club Drive, Santa Cruz
items.hours: Sunrise to 4 p.m. (Nov–Mar); sunrise to 7 p.m. (Apr–Oct)
items.description: City greenbelt preserve of meadows, woodland and creeks with about 11.5 miles of trails linking to UC Santa Cruz and Henry Cowell.
items.notes: Leashed dogs only on trails where allowed (Emma McCrary Trail yes). Bikes only on the multi-use trail and Emma McCrary Trail. Fee not stated on the city page.

items.name: Moore Creek Preserve
items.address: Moore Creek Preserve, Santa Cruz, CA
items.hours: Sunrise to 4 p.m. (Nov–Mar); sunrise to 7 p.m. (Apr–Oct)
items.best_time: Spring for wildflowers.
items.description: Hiking-only city preserve on the west side with about 2.5 miles round trip of trails through coastal prairie and meadows with Monterey Bay views.
items.notes: Walk-in entrances at Highway 1 across from Shaffer Road and at the end of Meder Street; no on-site parking. Not wheelchair accessible.

items.name: Arana Gulch
items.hours: One hour before sunrise to one hour after sunset
items.description: City open space near the harbor with a paved multi-use trail and dirt loops through meadows, wetlands and habitat for the Santa Cruz tarplant.
items.notes: Leashed dogs on all trails except Marsh Vista Trail; bikes only on the paved trail. No on-site parking (street parking on Agnes Street).

items.name: DeLaveaga Park
items.cost: Free park entry; golf and disc golf parking pass extra
items.description: Large city park in the hills with hiking and bike trails, a disc golf course, an archery range and a golf course.
items.notes: George Washington Grove closed for winter, Nov 1–Mar 1. Archery range vehicle gates open only noon–4 p.m. weekends.

items.name: Capitola Village & Capitola Beach
items.address: Capitola Village & Capitola Beach, Capitola, CA
items.description: Neighboring seaside city whose village centers on Capitola Beach, the Esplanade and the Capitola Wharf.
items.notes: No dogs on Capitola Beach. The beach and wharf close during high surf.

items.name: Big Basin Redwoods State Park
items.address: 20580 Big Basin Way, Boulder Creek, CA 95006
items.cost: $10 per vehicle; $6 + $2 reservation fee with a day-use parking reservation
items.best_time: Reserve day-use parking ahead; spaces are limited.
items.description: Redwood park recovering from the 2020 CZU Lightning Complex Fire, where most old-growth redwoods survived.
items.notes: All campgrounds are closed while the park rebuilds from the 2020 fire; it also closes during wind advisories. No day-use parking for oversized vehicles.

items.name: Año Nuevo State Park (elephant seals)
items.address: 1 New Years Creek Rd, Pescadero, CA 94060
items.cost: $10 per vehicle ($9 seniors 62+); guided walks reserved via ReserveCalifornia
items.hours: 8:30 a.m. to sunset; seal viewing areas 8:30 a.m.–3:30 p.m.
items.best_time: Dec 15–Mar 31 breeding season: guided walks only, reserve up to 56 days ahead. Apr 1–Nov 30: self-guided with a free permit issued 8:30 a.m.–3:30 p.m.
items.description: Coastal state park north of Santa Cruz where elephant seals can be seen on guided walks in winter and with a free permit the rest of the year.
items.notes: Wildlife Viewing Area closed Dec 1–14 each year. No public tours Jan 23–24, 2027. No pets, drones or strollers in viewing areas (Dec–Mar); no camping.

items.name: Roaring Camp Railroads
items.cost: Redwood Forest Steam Train: adults $42.35; children 2–12 $26.45; under 2 free
items.description: Narrated 75-minute steam train ride through the redwoods to the summit of Bear Mountain.
items.notes: Santa Cruz Beach Train (to the Boardwalk) is not running — marked 'Returning Spring 2027'. Schedule and prices subject to change.

items.name: Elkhorn Slough Ecological Reserve
items.hours: Wed–Sun 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; closed Mon & Tue
items.description: State ecological reserve on Elkhorn Slough with about 5 miles of trails in three loops, including a 0.6-mile paved, ADA-compliant Overlook Trail.
items.notes: Closed Mondays and Tuesdays; no dogs. Check in at the visitor center before hiking.

items.name: Monterey Bay Aquarium
items.hours: Open daily except Christmas Day; hours vary by season
items.best_time: Buy tickets in advance.
items.description: Public aquarium on Cannery Row in Monterey, across the bay from Santa Cruz.

items.name: Pigeon Point Light Station State Historic Park
items.address: 210 Pigeon Point Road, Highway 1, Pescadero, CA 94060
items.hours: Day use 8am to sunset; visitor center Thu–Tue 10am–4pm as staffing permits
items.description: Historic coastal light station south of Pescadero whose original Fresnel lens is displayed in the Fog Signal Building.
items.notes: The tower is closed for restoration; you can see it from the grounds. No dogs or drones.

items.name: Seacliff State Beach
items.description: State beach in Aptos with a promenade, covered picnic areas and a visitor center; the concrete ship SS Palo Alto lies offshore and is closed to visitors.
items.notes: SS Palo Alto concrete ship closed to the public; the pier was destroyed in 2023 storms and removed; campground closed pending rebuild. No alcohol; leashed dogs allowed.

items.name: The Forest of Nisene Marks State Park
items.address: The Forest of Nisene Marks State Park, Aptos, CA
items.description: State park four miles north of Aptos with about 30 miles of hiking, biking and jogging trails along Aptos Creek.
items.notes: Aptos Creek Trail, Five Finger Falls trail and West Ridge Trail Camp closed due to storm damage. No parking on Aptos Creek Road; camping unavailable; dogs and bikes limited to lower areas.

items.name: Santa Cruz Museum of Art & History (MAH)
items.cost: Suggested $10 general; $8 seniors, students, teachers, veterans; free for members and children under 5
items.best_time: Thursday or Friday evening, open until 8pm
items.description: Downtown museum of art and local history, entered from Front Street or the Abbott Square plaza. Admission is a suggested price; special ticketed exhibitions and events are priced separately.
items.notes: Admission is a suggested donation.

items.name: Santa Cruz Museum of Natural History
items.address: 1305 E Cliff Dr, Santa Cruz, CA 95062
items.cost: $5 adults; $3 seniors 60+ and college students; free under 18 and members
items.hours: Tue-Wed 11am-4pm; Sat-Sun 10am-5pm; closed Mon, Thu, Fri
items.best_time: Weekend mornings
items.description: Small natural history museum on East Cliff Drive focused on the region's plants, animals and geology. Visitors under 18 get in free.
items.notes: Closed the day after Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve and Day, New Year's Eve and Day.

items.name: UC Santa Cruz Arboretum & Botanic Garden
items.cost: $13 adults; $10 seniors 65+; $7 youth 4-17; under 4 free; free on First Tuesday
items.best_time: First Tuesday of the month (free Community Day)
items.description: University botanic garden on the UCSC campus with gardens open daily. Admission is free for everyone on the first Tuesday of each month.
items.notes: Free on the first Tuesday of the month. Closed 24 December 2026 to 1 January 2027.

items.name: Santa Cruz Public Libraries — Downtown Branch
items.best_time: Any open day; good rainy-day stop downtown
items.description: The main downtown branch of the county's public library system, a short walk from Pacific Avenue. Free and open seven days a week.

items.name: Bookshop Santa Cruz
items.best_time: Evenings; check the events calendar for author talks
items.description: Independent bookstore on Pacific Avenue that also hosts author events and readings. Browsing is free.
items.notes: The shop's own pages list different hours; closed Christmas Day and New Year's Day.

items.name: Harvey West Park
items.best_time: Dry afternoons
items.description: Large city park north of downtown with playground equipment, ball fields and picnic areas. The adjacent Harvey West Pool opens to the public seasonally.
items.notes: The Harvey West Pool next door runs lap swim only in winter.

items.name: Depot Park
items.best_time: Dry afternoons
items.description: City park with a playground, a bike park, soccer fields and a plaza area, plus restrooms and picnic tables.
items.notes: Parking lots are pay-for-use (no rates listed). Dogs leashed; not on artificial turf.

items.name: Ken Wormhoudt Skate Park (Mike Fox Park)
items.address: 225 San Lorenzo Blvd at Riverside Avenue, Santa Cruz, CA 95060
items.best_time: Dry days
items.description: Concrete city skate park at Mike Fox Park beside the San Lorenzo River. Helmets, elbow pads and knee pads are required; bikes and scooters are not allowed.
items.notes: Closes when wet.

items.name: Downtown Santa Cruz (Pacific Avenue district)
items.address: Downtown Santa Cruz (Pacific Avenue district), Santa Cruz (Downtown), CA
items.best_time: Evenings and First Friday; holiday events late Nov-Dec
items.description: The city's walkable core along and around Pacific Avenue, with shops, restaurants, bars and several of the city's music venues and cinemas. The Downtown Association runs the district's events calendar.

items.name: Abbott Square Market
items.address: 725 Front Street & 118 Cooper Street, Santa Cruz, CA
items.best_time: Evenings for free live music
items.description: Food hall in the MAH's outdoor plaza at Front and Cooper streets, with several restaurants and bars around shared seating. The market advertises free live music.
items.notes: Closed Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve and Christmas Day; open to midnight on New Year's Eve.

items.name: Downtown Santa Cruz Farmers' Market
items.address: Cedar St & Church St, Santa Cruz, CA
items.best_time: Wednesday afternoon
items.description: Year-round Wednesday market of the Santa Cruz Community Farmers' Markets, held rain or shine. It has moved to Cedar and Church streets, a short distance from its former lot.
items.notes: The operator says it starts at 12:30pm; the City says 1pm.

site_link.label: Every Santa Cruz County farmers market

items.name: Westside Santa Cruz Farmers' Market
items.address: Mission St. Ext. and Western Dr., Santa Cruz, CA
items.best_time: Saturday morning
items.description: Year-round Saturday morning farmers market on the Westside, run by the Santa Cruz Community Farmers' Markets.
items.notes: Year-round.

site_link.label: Every Santa Cruz County farmers market

items.name: Live Oak/Eastside Farmers' Market
items.address: 15th Ave & East Cliff Dr, Santa Cruz, CA
items.best_time: Sunday morning
items.description: Year-round Sunday morning market in Live Oak, just east of the Santa Cruz city line, operated by the Santa Cruz Community Farmers' Markets.
items.notes: In Live Oak, just east of the city.

site_link.label: Every Santa Cruz County farmers market

items.name: The Catalyst
items.best_time: Show nights; karaoke Fri-Sat 9pm-1am
items.description: Long-running Pacific Avenue concert venue with a main room and the smaller Atrium. Age limits vary by show, commonly 16+ or 18+.
items.notes: Age limits vary by show.

site_link.label: New Year's Eve in Santa Cruz

items.name: Kuumbwa Jazz Center
items.best_time: Weeknight concerts; free winter master classes
items.description: Downtown jazz performance and education venue with a cafe serving dinner specials on show nights. It also offers free master classes, in person or streamed.

items.name: Moe's Alley
items.best_time: Show nights (typically doors 7pm, show 8pm)
items.description: 21-and-over live music club with a full bar and outdoor patio. Food at most shows comes from a partner taqueria.
items.notes: Buy tickets from the club's site or Ticketweb only.

items.name: Rio Theatre
items.best_time: Event nights
items.description: Single-room performing arts venue on Soquel Avenue that hosts concerts, film and other live events.

items.name: Del Mar Theatre (Landmark)
items.best_time: Rainy afternoons or evenings
items.description: Art deco cinema on Pacific Avenue built in 1936, now a three-screen Landmark Theatres location showing independent and foreign-language films with beer and wine.

items.name: Santa Cruz Civic Auditorium
items.hours: Box office Tue-Fri 12-4pm; opens 90 min before events
items.best_time: Symphony and touring show nights
items.description: City-owned downtown auditorium across from City Hall that hosts the Santa Cruz Symphony, Cabrillo Festival and other events. Tickets also sell online.

items.name: Santa Cruz Warriors at Kaiser Permanente Arena
items.hours: Game days; box office opens 1.5 hours before tip-off
items.best_time: Home game nights during the 2026-27 G League season
items.description: Downtown arena where the Santa Cruz Warriors play all home games. Single-game, season and group tickets are sold through the team.
items.notes: Bags must be under 14×14×6 inches; no backpacks or coolers.

items.name: Santa Cruz Shakespeare
items.address: 501 Upper Park Road, Santa Cruz, CA 95065
items.hours: Summer festival mid-July to early Oct at The Grove @ DeLaveaga Park; A Christmas Carol Dec 3-24, 2026 at the Veterans Memorial Building
items.best_time: Summer evenings at the outdoor Grove; December for A Christmas Carol
items.description: Professional theatre company staging a summer-fall festival outdoors in DeLaveaga Park's Audrey Stanley Grove, plus a downtown holiday production of A Christmas Carol.
items.notes: The summer festival runs outdoors from mid-July to mid-October; A Christmas Carol runs 3–24 December 2026.
